div.head: III Eg 7.3
div.ab: ⁊ geséce se æbæra ðeof ðæt þæt he gesece, oþþe se ðe on hlafordsearwe gemet sie, þæt hi næfre feorh ne gesecen.
⁊ gesece se æbæra ðeof þæt þæt he gesece, oððe se þe on hlafordsearwe gemet sy, þæt hi næfre feorh na geseceon.
⁊ gesece se æbæra þeof þæt þæt he gesece, oððe se þe on hlafordsearwe gemet sy, þæt hy næfre feorh gesecan.
Et querat fur quicquid querat, uel qui de morte domini sui cogitauerit, nunquam sibi uitam perquirat.
⁊ gesece se æbæra þeof þæt þæt he gesece, oððe se þe on hlafordsearwe gemet sy, þæt hi næfre feorh ne gesecan, buton se cyningc him feorhgeneres unne.
And gesece se æbæra ðeof ðæt þæt he gesece, oþþe se ðe on hlafordsearwe gemet sie, þæt hi næfre feorh ne gesecen.
And the proved thief, or he who has been discovered in treason against his lord, whatever refuge he seeks, shall never be able to save his life, unless the king grant that it be spared.
And anyone convicted of theft or caught conspiring against his lord shall not be able to save his life, no matter where he hides.
And no matter what refuge the proved thief, or the man who is discovered in treason against his lord, may reach, they are never to save their lives.

Und der offenkundige Dieb oder wer auf Verrath gegen seinen Herrn betroffen ist, mag [von Asylen] aufsuchen, was er immer aufsuche: dass sie niemals das Leben [gesichert] erlangen (ausser wenn ihnen der König Lebensrettung vergönnt D).

And let the manifest thief, or whoever is found guilty of treachery against his lord, seek [sanctuary] wherever he may: they are never to obtain [security of] life (unless the king grants them their life, D).
div.note: D adds ‘buton se cyninge him feorhgeneres unne’.
The Corpus MS. adds: “unless the king allows them to preserve their life”.
gesecen: D adds buton se cyninge him feorhgeneres unne
no matter where he hides: Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 201 adds, “unless the king allows him to be spared” (buton se cyninge him feorhgeneres unne). 8–8.3 Likely an addition by Wulfstan.
